result.question:
I'm worried that urgent work on Transformer 1 at site MAIN is stuck behind an overloaded technician. Give me the MAIN site's work order KPIs for the last 6 months, including backlog, overdue count and average completion time. Then list every open work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority, scheduled date and assigned technician, and flag which ones are overdue.

For each technician assigned to those work orders, count how many open work orders they currently hold at MAIN. Anyone holding more than 5 counts as overloaded.

Next, work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630.

If Transformer 1 is at Condition 2 or higher, do the following for any overdue work order on it that sits with an overloaded technician. Reassign it to the technician with the fewest open work orders at MAIN, choosing among those who have worked on Transformer 1 before and are not overloaded. Give it a start date within the next 7 days that avoids any day with 3 or more scheduled work orders at MAIN. If it is Condition 1, don't reassign anything. Just list the overdue items and recommend a catch-up order, ranked by priority and then by how late they are.

If every technician with Transformer 1 history is overloaded, don't reassign. Tell me who is least loaded and recommend bringing in outside help. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.
result.answer:
I made no changes: nothing met the reassignment rule. Transformer 1 is at DGA Condition 4, well above your Condition 2 trigger. But neither of its open work orders has a technician assigned, neither has a scheduled date, and no technician has ever worked on Transformer 1.

**1. MAIN work order KPIs (last 6 months)**
- Total: 2 (both on Transformer 1). Completed: 0.
- Backlog: 2
- Overdue: 0
- Average completion time: 0 hrs, because nothing has been completed in the period.
- Priority mix: one P1, one P3.

**2. Open work orders on Transformer 1**

| WO | Description | Priority | Status | Scheduled start | Technician | Overdue? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection: on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | WAPPR | None | None | Not by the system fields ⚠️ |
| 1000052 | Oil sample retest (DGA) and insulation check for T2 thermal fault | 3 | APPR | None (notes say target 2026-10-01) | None | No |

⚠️ On 1000051, the system has no scheduled or target date, so it doesn't count as overdue in the KPIs. However, its notes give a target start of 2024-01-19, which is about 2.7 years ago. It is also still waiting for approval (WAPPR). In practice it is your stuck urgent job.

**3. Technician load**
- Nobody is assigned to either Transformer 1 work order, so there are no technicians to count.
- For reference, MAIN has 4 open work orders in total. The only assigned technicians are MECHTECH2 (1 open, on PUMP3) and HVACTECH1 (1 open, on CHILLER6).
- Nobody at MAIN holds more than 5, so nobody is overloaded.

**4. TDCG from the latest oil sample (2024-01-19)**
- Gases in ppm: H₂ 2850 + CH₄ 7400 + C₂H₆ 5470 + C₂H₄ 16650 + C₂H₂ 7 + CO 32 = **32,409 ppm**
- That is **Condition 4** (above 4630).
- All six gases had values, so nothing was carried forward.
- This sample is about 2.7 years old; the sensor feed has nothing newer.

**5. Why nothing was reassigned**
- No work order on Transformer 1 is overdue by date and sitting with an overloaded technician.
- There is also nobody to reassign to: no technician has Transformer 1 history, which the work order notes confirm. Your fallback rule applies.
- The least-loaded technicians at MAIN are MECHTECH2 and HVACTECH1, with 1 open work order each. Neither has transformer experience; they are mechanical and HVAC crafts.
- **Recommendation:** bring in an outside transformer or electrical specialist.
- There is room in the schedule: MAIN has 0 work orders scheduled from 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-07, so any day that week works.

**6. Suggested catch-up order**
1. **WO 1000051 (P1, OLTC inspection):** approve it now, then assign the outside specialist with a start date in the next few days. It is about 2.7 years late against the target date in its notes.
2. **WO 1000052 (P3, DGA retest and insulation check):** keep the 2026-10-01 target in its notes. A fresh oil sample matters because 32,409 ppm is severe and the last sample is years old.

If you'd like, I can approve 1000051 and assign both work orders to a contractor labor code with dates in that open week.
